parsed.why: Worst-tier state: birth-certificate markers effectively closed, 2023 law restricts trans bathroom use in state-run facilities, hate-crime statute omits gender identity, no statewide anti-discrimination. Documented hostile legislation plus hostile facilities rule drops it well below the 0.35 national line.

Low-risk tier: enforced gender-identity protections in employment, housing and accommodations, remedies ordered, open ID markers, city sanctuary order shielding visitors' care access. No bathroom ban; only state gaps are LGBT hate-crime coverage and pending youth sport bills. Sits clearly above the parent line.

No local bathroom ban but a national-legislature-imposed facilities restriction, federal override of local law, protesters arrested 2024, and dossier resolves nothing on local police, hate-crime or custody. Protective reputation documented but not durable; only modestly above parent.

Facility restriction covers public-school students only, no adult bathroom rule, but minors' care ban in force, surgical requirement for certificate amendment, hate-crime statute excludes gender identity, protections municipal only. Below the national line, above slot 1.

Most-protective tier: statutory gender-identity protections including accommodations upheld by ballot, hate-crime coverage with reporting machinery, self-declared IDs, care shield law protecting visitors. Only unrepealed unenforceable sodomy wording and retained national border regime hold it down.
